reply_text:
㊥ ("one system … WEFT, WARP, TAPESTRY") Agreed on the first part, and I want the futon6 terms exact before I map them, so let me read what WARP, WEFT and TAPESTRY name there.㊣ ("one system … a session is an interesting efficiency") Agreed, and the futon6 terms fit closely once read from their own definitions. Recorded in the mission with your words verbatim (44b60892); claude-15 told not to adopt the session-end marks.

🈖 (the mapping) In futon6 the weft is the per-paper markup pass, the warp is the cross-corpus substrate per concept (concordance, citations, where each concept is defined), and the tapestry is the per-concept phylogeny over the citation graph, typed definition / cited activation / uncited activation / redefinition, which the breakdown calls "git-blame for a concept". Here:
- **Weft** is what 象 does now: the per-session reading, acts and ports and closes within a turn and its session. The record fields are weft output. Session end is a weft boundary, which is why it closes nothing.
- **Warp** is per subject across all sessions and seats: where an ask, a standing rule, an entity or a mission occurs. minus40's mentions and facts by subject are warp; the mission id the records lack is the missing warp thread for turns. The accumulator you asked about is warp maintenance, incremental per subject, replacing the per-session recompute as the unit grows.
- **Tapestry** is per-item descent: first said, explicitly linked, inferred, superseded. The four futon6 edge types map one to one onto opens / quote-bracket or carries-out link / sole-port witness / retraction or memory version. The `:xiang/answers` and `:xiang/scope` hyperedges are tapestry edges, and the resume brief is a tapestry read over a mission's open items.

㊢ (what changes in the lane) The session-end path stays as a recorded fact and stops closing ports; lapsed, orphaned and unread are withdrawn as inbox states. Nothing is wrong live, since no session has ended since the reload. claude-15 was switching fault intake to the marks on the first real record; I have asked them not to.

㊭ (first two packets, each one file, ready to send on your word) Stamp the seat's mission id onto every turn record at write time, which gives the warp thread; and a classical brief generator over a mission's records and facts, with an Emacs command that inserts it at the top of a fresh REPL. Then we run it on this REPL and count re-asks. That is the demo.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-16
previous_reply_acts.text: ("what is needed to see this working") A demo exists the moment one thing is built that nobody has built yet: a resume brief in the agent's first prompt. Everything the brief reads is now stored. The classifier improves the brief; it does not gate it. And on session end, you are right, and I will say so plainly below. Let me ground one claim first: whether a conversation can be joined across sessions from what the records already carry.㊢ (checked, and a correction of my own earlier claim) The turn records carry no mission or excursion field at all, across 3,735 records. The join I named two evenings ago, "every chat turn carries its clocked target", is not on the records; the mission id lives on the roster per seat (15 seats on M-象-2000 right now) and would have to be stamped onto each record at write time. I could not reach the evidence query route to check the chat-turn evidence either. So the first thing a demo needs is a one-field change: the turn service writes the seat's mission id onto the record. Without it there is no conversation, only sessions.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-16
previous_reply_acts.text:
("what is needed to see this working") Your acceptance sense was: jumping into an agent chat feels like continuing a familiar conversation. The demo that shows it is a resume brief placed in the agent's first prompt, and then you ask something and watch whether it re-asks. Four pieces, three of them small:
1. **Mission id on the record** (above). Then "conversation" is classical: all records whose seat was on M-X, across sessions and agents.
2. **A brief generator**, classical, reading the fields that went live yesterday: open ports with their witness or "no answer linked", standings in force, obligations, plus minus40's facts about the mission's entities with referent dates, plus the operator-voice anchor from the mission file. No model.
3. **Delivery**: an Emacs command that inserts the brief at the top of a fresh REPL buffer, or the session-mode hook that composes the first prompt. Either is a few lines on the voxterm/session-mode side.
4. **The measure**: count of re-asks in the first turn after resume, over real resumes. It can fail.
The classifier is not on this path. It makes the brief more honest about "answered" against "addressed, still owed", which is the 368-of-758 finding; the brief can show the witness and let you judge until then.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-16
previous_reply_acts.text: ("lots has been done without any interactive demo") Agreed, and it is the pattern of the last three days: the record side was built to the spec and checked by recompute totals, and nobody has yet looked at it as a user. The inbox page is a ten-minute rebuild, not a thing you sit in front of. The brief is the first artifact that puts the stored state in front of a reader at the moment it matters.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-16
previous_reply_acts.text: ("would an 'end' really be needed") No, and the reason is the same unit problem. Lapsed and orphaned presume that the session is the conversation: an agent port lapses because that agent's session is gone, an operator ask is orphaned because nobody in that session will answer. With the conversation as the unit, neither follows. The next seat on the mission can answer the agent's port; your ask is not orphaned, it is open and goes into the next brief. The real ends are: answered, withdrawn by you, or stale by time, and staleness is a judgment at read time ("open since 3 October"), not a stored state change. What I built yesterday records a true fact, that the registry changed a session id, and the system-record mechanism is reusable. But the lapse and orphan readings of that fact should not reach the inbox as states. I would keep the outbox, stop treating a session change as closing anything, and let the brief carry open items forward. claude-15's fault-intake switch to reading the marks should not happen; I will tell them.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-16
previous_reply_acts.text: ("efficient accumulator") The kernel already answers "what is open as of now" from the act database, but it recomputes over the whole session on every turn, with a cap of ten thousand records. Over a conversation spanning sessions that cost grows, and the incremental form is a fold: each settled record updates a stored open set, standings and obligations for its conversation, which is what the hyperedge carrier in futon1b is for. The brief reads the accumulated state; the fold replaces both the per-turn recompute and the session-end act.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-16
previous_reply_acts.text: (order I would take) Mission id on the record, then the brief and its Emacs delivery, then run it on this REPL and on claude-15's, which have the longest histories, and count re-asks. Classifier after that, trained on the 1,540 incidences, feeding the brief's answered/kept distinction and then the kernel's effect rule. Session end demoted as above. If you agree I will write the first two packets; they are each one file.
